newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch closing debt market report.
newsitem.headline: Dutch closing debt market report.

text.p: Dutch bonds closed slightly higher on Monday, off morning peaks, but above midsession levels hit when market players reacted to renewed EMU-worries.
Activity focused on futures trade, done by professional traders, with most end-investors staying sidelined throughout the session.
"At the moment, the market is at a level far too high for them," one dealer said.
"As you get higher, yields get lower and end-investors get rarer," another commented.
One dealer said proprietary trade was mainly done in futures, as it enabled an easy reshuffling of positions.
"Dealers get into futures, because they can get out at any time," he said.
He said the cash market had been quiet overall, but added there seemed to have been some switching between bonds maturing in 2010 and in 2023.
Dealers later played down the importance of French statements asking for extra time to study the stability pact, which is planned to keep budget deficits tight once the euro is launched.
